gen_risks.description: Escalating conflict and violence in the region may disrupt project activities, limit access to target areas and endanger staff.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain security liaison, develop flexible implementation plans, pre‑position supplies, and activate contingency protocols with local authorities.
gen_risks.evidence: Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence… regional conflicts, such as Boko Haram attacks in Cameroon and ongoing unrest in CAR (Section A2).

gen_risks.description: Delays in recruiting required PIU specialists (accountant, environmental, gender‑based violence, etc.) could stall project start‑up.
gen_risks.mitigation: Launch early recruitment drives, use temporary contracts, and provide incentives to attract qualified staff before the effectiveness date.
gen_risks.evidence: Recipient shall appoint, assign, or recruit an accountant, a knowledge management… specialist no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date (Legal Covenants).

gen_risks.description: Weak financial management capacity leads to inaccurate reporting, misallocation of funds and audit findings.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update FM manuals, customize accounting software, recruit internal and external auditors, and provide World Bank‑led FM training and supervision.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall FM residual risk rating is Substantial… FM risk assessment at concept for the project… rated as Substantial (Section 58‑59).

gen_risks.description: Procurement delays, weak contract management and limited market competition in fragile settings may cause cost overruns and schedule slips.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire experienced procurement specialists, conduct early market engagement, use STEP for real‑time monitoring, and strengthen contract‑management training.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management… mitigation measures include hiring experienced procurement specialists (Section 64‑65).

gen_risks.description: Construction and civil works generate waste, dust, emissions and occupational hazards that could affect nearby communities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare site‑specific ESMPs, enforce waste‑management plans, monitor air quality and provide PPE to workers.
gen_risks.evidence: Environmental risks are considered Substantial… impacts on water quality; disposal of building/construction wastes; occupational health and safety (Section 66).

gen_risks.description: Increased community health workforce raises risk of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEA/SH).
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct GBV/SEA risk assessments, recruit dedicated GBV specialists, train all staff on codes of conduct and establish reporting mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: Overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial… increased presence of new health workforce such as CHWs may create concerns of Sexual exploitation and abuse (Section 72‑73).

gen_risks.description: Climate change will increase vector‑borne diseases and flood‑related outbreaks, stressing health services and facilities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑resilient designs in health infrastructure, embed climate data into surveillance systems, and develop climate‑adaptation response plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change contributed to at least 50 % of natural disasters… increasing temperatures expanding malaria‑transmitting mosquitoes (Section 11).

gen_risks.description: Low domestic health financing and high out‑of‑pocket spending threaten long‑term sustainability of interventions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Support domestic resource mobilization, integrate health security into national budgets, and assist governments in developing medium‑term expenditure frameworks.
gen_risks.evidence: Cameroon’s domestic funding for health per capita was US$10.79… high reliance on out‑of‑pocket payments (61 %) (Annex 2).

gen_risks.description: Governance weaknesses at national level may slow decision‑making and impede coordinated implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen steering committees, provide governance capacity‑building, and establish clear reporting lines and timelines.
gen_risks.evidence: Key risks to successful implementation… governance challenges, economic constraints, and environmental vulnerabilities (Section 16).

gen_risks.description: Failure to sign the MoU with WOAH within 90 days could limit regional animal health coordination.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set internal deadline reminders, monitor compliance, and engage legal support to expedite MoU finalisation.
gen_risks.evidence: Recipient shall, no later than ninety (90) days after the Effective Date, enter into a Memorandum of Understanding with WOAH (Legal Covenants).

gen_risks.description: Disruptions in global supply chains may delay delivery of vaccines, diagnostics and PPE needed for emergencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish buffer stocks, diversify suppliers, and develop logistics contingency plans with regional hubs.
gen_risks.evidence: Support to access countermeasures through strengthening emergency logistics and supply chains, including stockpiling (Component 3.1).

gen_risks.description: Fragmented data systems across human, animal and environmental sectors hinder real‑time surveillance and decision‑making.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop an interoperable digital platform, adopt common data standards, and train staff on integrated use of DHIS2 and LIMS.
gen_risks.evidence: Developing interoperable digital platform… integration of OH data using DHIS2 (Annex 1, Subcomponent 2.1).

gen_risks.description: Under‑representation of women in technical epidemiology and veterinary roles limits gender‑responsive capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set gender quotas, conduct outreach to female candidates, and provide flexible training formats.
gen_risks.evidence: Women remain underrepresented… project targets women training in FETP and veterinary fields (Section 75‑76).

gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder engagement may exclude vulnerable groups, leading to grievances and project delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement robust GRM, conduct inclusive consultations, and adapt the Umbrella Stakeholder Engagement Plan to national contexts.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups… citizen engagement mechanisms such as consultations and GRMs (Section 71‑74).

gen_risks.description: Security threats to staff operating in FCV zones could cause injuries or evacuation, halting activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare country‑specific Security Risk Assessments and Management Plans, provide security training and insurance, and adjust field schedules as needed.
gen_risks.evidence: PIUs of FCV countries will also prepare a country‑specific Security Risk Assessment (SRA) and Security Risk Management Plan (SMP) (Section 73).

gen_risks.description: Customising existing accounting software after the effectiveness date may be delayed, affecting financial reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Award IT contract early, set milestone‑based delivery schedule, and conduct user‑acceptance testing before go‑live.
gen_risks.evidence: Customize the existing accounting software… no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date (Legal Covenants).

gen_risks.description: High turnover of health workers due to displacement and insecurity reduces programme continuity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer retention incentives, remote training options, and establish backup staffing pools.
gen_risks.evidence: Over 1.5 million IDPs and refugees… internal displacement affecting health workforce (Section 3).

gen_risks.description: Poor quality or untimely M&E data could impede performance tracking and decision‑making.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen M&E capacity, conduct regular data quality audits, and use standardized reporting templates.
gen_risks.evidence: PIUs will be responsible for M&E… ensure data harmonized and comparable (Section B).

gen_risks.description: Inadequate biosafety in laboratories may cause accidental pathogen exposure or contamination.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement biosafety training, certify labs to SLIPTA standards, and enforce strict SOPs for sample handling.
gen_risks.evidence: Laboratory Quality and Capacity subcomponent includes biosafety & biosecurity (Section 30).

gen_risks.description: Non‑compliance with ESF safeguards could trigger World Bank suspensions or project delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finalize ESCP, LMP and SEP early, conduct regular E&S monitoring, and remediate any non‑compliance promptly.
gen_risks.evidence: Project prepared under ESF… environmental risks substantial… site‑specific ESMPs required (Section 65‑66).

gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic instability may limit government ability to meet co‑financing commitments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Negotiate flexible financing arrangements, maintain contingency reserves, and coordinate with development partners for supplemental funding.
gen_risks.evidence: Challenging macro‑fiscal outlook and high poverty levels make the region vulnerable to shocks (Section A2).

gen_risks.description: Procurement fraud or corruption could erode trust and waste resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply World Bank Anti‑Fraud and Corruption Guidelines, conduct independent audits, and enforce strict vendor vetting.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement will follow World Bank Procurement Regulations… Anti‑Fraud and Corruption Guidelines (Section 62).

gen_risks.description: Delay in preparing the Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) manual and emergency action plan may hinder rapid fund deployment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop CERC manual and EAP within the first six months, obtain Bank approval early, and train staff on activation procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: CERC component… Government will prepare a CERC Manual, submit an emergency action plan (Section 35).

gen_risks.description: Weak coordination among multiple ministries and agencies can cause duplication and inefficiencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear terms of reference for the National Steering Committee and Technical Committee, and hold regular joint coordination meetings.
gen_risks.evidence: Implementation under respective Ministries… PIU will coordinate… national steering committee and technical committee will oversee (Section 44‑45).

gen_risks.description: Improper handling of medical and laboratory waste may contaminate the environment and pose health hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt the National Healthcare Waste Management Plan, train staff on waste segregation, and monitor disposal practices.
gen_risks.evidence: Project will take advantage of the existing National Healthcare Waste Management Plan… (Section 23).

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
